entities.summary: The Cetina culture is the name for the culture of the inhabitants of the Middle Dalmatian coast, and especially its hinterland, during the early Bronze Age, or, according to Paul Reineck's chronology. It is named after the numerous sites along the Cetina river in Central Dalmatia and Herzegovina. People of this culture were present in caves or in open settlements. The graves are in rocky colonies. In the case of inhumation, they have the shape of a stone chest, while incinerated remains of the deceased are laid in clay pots.
